title: AI-generated Steam capsule art for my solo indie game does the final version read best?
author: OptimaArch
selftext:
Solo dev here. I’ve been iterating on Steam capsule art for my pixel-art roguelike defense game.  
  
The art was created with AI and then refined through multiple iterations. I’m mainly trying to improve thumbnail readability, composition, and whether the capsule feels strong enough for Steam.  
  
The bottom one is my current final version.  
  
What do you think?  
\- Does the final version read best?  
\- Does it still feel too busy or too obviously AI-generated?

comments.author: HumanBotHybrid780
comments.body: You're going to have major issues if the characters overlap the green border.

replies.author: empty-microchip-2564
replies.body: yeah steam ui overlays like discount tags will completely cover that area. you definitely want to keep your main silhouettes strictly inside the safe zone so it still reads well when scaled down.

replies.author: OptimaArch
replies.body: Thanks for the feedback I will check it out!

comments.author: DairyDukes
comments.body: Close! Just switch that T to a P and you’ve nailed it!

replies.author: aigamedev-ModTeam
replies.body: Be respectful. Removed for AI Art or Artist bashing.

comments.author: Vlaxilla
comments.body: I prefer the 1st one but I guess on the last one you can see tbe slot clearer

comments.author: Trashy_io
comments.body: Looks great! Maybe try adding some light to the hole the slot s going in to? might help draw they eye to it and help get the game genre across quicker!

comments.author: BossRJM
comments.body: The "slotBound", sizing is a bit off, fine if intended, the "B" stands out. Otherwise, as others have said here.

replies.author: OptimaArch
replies.body:
Yep, that was intentional.

I wanted the "B" to stand out a bit more because it's the visual pivot of the logo. The idea is that the word can be mentally split into "Slot" and "Bound", which reflects the game's core theme: being bound by the fate of the slot machine.

So the larger "B" is there to subtly emphasize that transition and make the second half of the title more memorable at small thumbnail sizes.

replies.author: BossRJM
replies.body:
Fair enough, p.s. the archer looks like Link, I like that... May try it out!

Good luck!

comments.author: Ambitious-Crew-7132
comments.body:
It does give off strong AI vibes. What really caught my attention, though, were the goblins, they seem to be looking at a weird spot rather than at the knight. Maybe they're looking at the wizard, but even that feels awkward.

The border is also werid and doesn't fit the color palette at all. It would probably look better without it. I also can't see the entire elf's bow, which makes the composition feel weak.

The slot machine is cut off at the top, even though there's a lot of unused space in the image.
